function: Position-assisted beam prediction: an autoencoder maps the GPS position of the mobile unit to the best beam index of a 64-beam codebook at the BS (pp. 1-2).
system: Single-user mmWave ISAC testbed at 60 GHz; stationary BS with 16-element phased array, analog beamforming, 64-beam codebook; single-antenna mobile unit with GPS; no RIS (pp. 1-2).
method: Lightweight undercomplete autoencoder (LAE-424(32) selected), three layers, 2:1 compression; supervised on labeled position-beam pairs; batch size 16, learning rate 0.01, ReLU (pp. 2-4).
data_channel: Real-world DeepSense 6G data, nine scenarios from [7], 60 GHz, Arizona State University campus; GPS positions and received beam powers, public online (pp. 2-3).
test_conditions: Results per scenario for nine scenarios (day, night, rain; 854 to 5,964 samples) and codebook sizes 8 to 64; no cross-scenario test stated (pp. 3-5).
baselines: Learned only: FCN3(256), the three-layer fully connected network of [7]; no non-learned baseline compared (pp. 2-4).
metrics: Top-1 and top-k beam prediction accuracy, average power loss in dB, MinMaxDiff and MinAvgDiff accuracy gaps to baseline, MUL/ADD and parameter reduction (pp. 3-5).
complexity: Counts of parameters and multiplications/additions of dense layers; LAE-424(32) reduces MUL/ADD by 83.22% and parameters by 83.05% versus FCN3(256) (Table III, pp. 4-5).
openness: Public DeepSense 6G datasets (https://www.deepsense6g.net/data-collection/); main framework code stated public via [7]; no separate link to the LAE code (pp. 3, 5).
q1_support: p. 2: "we utilize the dataset from [7], which is part of the comprehensive DeepSense dataset for 6G learning research [9]"; p. 3: "the proposed model is trained on real-world data collected under these conditions". Met: measured DeepSense 6G data at 60 GHz.
q2_support: p. 2: "we trained and tested the models on nine datasets collected under diverse conditions". Not met: no experiment trains on one scenario and tests on another or adapts the model; results are per scenario (Fig. 4, p. 4) and per codebook size (Fig. 6, p. 5).
q3_support: p. 2: "We select FCN3(256), a three-layer NN with 256 hidden neurons, as a baseline" (footnote 1). Not met: it is the only comparison, an earlier learned method of [7], and no non-learned method (fixed, random or exhaustive beam) is compared anywhere.
q4_support: p. 4: "the highest complexity reduction of over 83% in terms of the number of multiplications, additions, and memory requirements, i.e., model parameters"; Table III (p. 5): MUL/ADD 83.22% and parameters 83.05% for LAE-424(32).
q5_support: p. 2: "we utilize the dataset from [7], which is part of the comprehensive DeepSense dataset for 6G learning research [9]"; p. 3, footnote 4: "the main framework code and the datasets employed in this study are publicly accessible online [7], [11]".
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match. Area 5 because the paper frames its system as mmWave ISAC (p. 1: "We consider a mmWave ISAC system"); the learned function is beam prediction from GPS position, so area 3 if the reviewer judges the link not to be ISAC. q2: the paper claims generalization across the nine scenarios (p. 2) but reports no model trained on one scenario and tested on another. q3: only FCN3(256) of [7] is compared. q4: Table III gives percentage reductions, with the count formulas on p. 4, not absolute counts. q5 rests on the public DeepSense 6G dataset; the framework code cited is that of [7].
